consensus_summary: Holy means sacred or set apart from the common/profane, especially as belonging or consecrated to God; the consensus also highlights moral purity and divine transcendence as contextual dimensions.
book_summary: Holy means set apart from what is common; created things are holy when claimed by God for an appointed purpose.
consensus_core_identification: Set apart from the common and belonging or consecrated to God.
book_core_identification: Set apart from the common and, for created things, claimed by God for a designated purpose.
boundary_disagreement: No material boundary disagreement. The book gives a compact consecrational formulation and does not separately discuss the moral-purity and divine-transcendence dimensions emphasized by the consensus, but it does not exclude them.
material_contradiction: None. The book directly preserves the consensus identification of holiness as distinction from the common and dedication or belonging to God.
rationale: After reducing both readings to their minimum cores, they identify the same category. The book’s phrase “claimed by God for an appointed purpose” is equivalent to the consensus language of belonging or being consecrated to God. Its brevity and emphasis on created things do not materially alter the referent or covered cases.
strongest_objection: The formulation may appear incomplete when applied to God himself, since the cited texts and definition primarily explain the holiness of created people or things and do not explicitly articulate divine moral perfection or transcendence. This is an omission of elaboration rather than a competing core meaning.
